newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara sells dollar/ringgit after baht float.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara sells dollar/ringgit after baht float.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia sold the dollar early on Wednesday after the Bank of Thailand said it would allow a managed float of the baht, dealers said.
But dealers said it was a token resistance set by the central bank at 2.5250 ringgit to the dollar.
"Negara came out himself to sell the dollar instead of normal exercise of proxy," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.

This is the first time in years that Bank Negara has used its own name while intervening in the foreign exchange market. It usually uses a broker or some of Malaysia's biggest banks for its operations, dealers said.
They said Bank Negara was present in the market right from New York on Tuesday evening to Sydney time this morning. It was checking rates through one of Malaysia's big banks.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers believed the amount of dollars sold by Bank Negara was small.
No confirmation was available from the central bank, which does not usually comment on its intervention operations.
The ringgit slipped to 2.5250 a dollar from its opening around 2.5230/35 after the Thai news and corresponding sell-down in the baht. But Bank Negara's presence helped reverse the ringgit's trend.
At 0400 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5225/35 to a dollar.

Thailand's Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday that effective immediately the country's exchange rate system would be a managed float, whereby the value of the baht would be set by market forces.
